analysis.title: Fed holds, but Treasuries rally on safety (Fixed Income Weekly Commentary, 02 November 2026)
key_insights: The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% in a 10-2 vote with hawkish undertones, citing a strong economy and elevated inflation.

Treasuries bull steepened: the 2-year fell 9 bps to 4.59%, the 10-year fell 7 bps to 4.93%, the 30-year fell 1 bp to 5.31%. Safe-haven demand tied to Middle East concerns and U.S. midterm election anxiety drove the front end.
Brent crude rose to $117 on concerns the U.S. may resume strikes against Iran. Nuveen names energy prices as the key risk to its outlook because they could pass into core inflation.
Nuveen expects one more Fed hike at the December meeting, then an extended hold through 2027. It calls this path less hawkish than current market pricing.
Nuveen forecasts the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.95% for year-end 2026 and 4.75% for end-2027, and the 2-year at 4.70% this year and 4.50% next year.

Every major fixed income sector except convertibles posted a positive total return, reversing two weeks of credit weakness. MBS and high yield were the best performers relative to similar-duration Treasuries.

Municipals rallied for a third week and closed their strongest month since November 2023. The Bloomberg Municipal Index returned +0.66% with a yield of 4.21%. Nuveen favors longer municipal duration over Treasuries.

Investment grade credit whipsawed on AI infrastructure return-on-investment anxiety and disappointing earnings. TMT spreads reached decade-wide levels. Issuance passed an all-time annual record, with weekly supply near double dealer forecasts, and investors were net sellers across the curve.

High yield ended the week mixed: higher-quality credits held firm while higher-beta names gave back ground as decompression returned after several technology earnings misses. High yield funds saw outflows for a sixth straight week.
Nuveen reads the recent firming in high yield and mortgages as a sign that the AI-driven credit decompression was sentiment-driven rather than fundamental.
Technology stocks sold off sharply into the week's end after a disappointing semiconductor revenue report.
Brazilian corporate and local-currency bonds fell after an unexpected election result, and Brazil lagged other EM markets.

sector_views.rationale: Nuveen favors longer duration in municipals over Treasuries. The index yields 4.21%, high yield municipals 5.87%, and 30-year municipals look cheap versus Treasuries.
Yields near 5.56% attract crossover investors, and Nuveen sees the backdrop as a chance to lock in elevated yields at attractive valuations.
Nuveen continues to favor high-quality income and says credit fundamentals remain sound.
